methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 11 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Neuromeka is a public robotics and manufacturing company listed on KOSDAQ, having raised $36.5M in total capital. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of nine firms across robotics and manufacturing—one public peer (ticker 277810.KQ) and eight private companies including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics.

The peer-median approach proved inapplicable due to insufficient narrow-set filtering. While 11 same-sector peers exist in robotics and manufacturing, none satisfied tight stage-alignment or valuation-tier criteria needed to produce three or more reliable datapoints. Applying an all-sector median would introduce material distortion given stage and business model variance. Consequently, this analysis cannot rely on conventional multiples triangulation without risking false precision.

The data constraints limit the analytical toolkit available. A robust valuation synthesis would require either: (1) expanded private comparables with detailed financial metrics from the eight identified peers, or (2) explicit multiples and profitability data from the single public comparable. Without these inputs, no credible range can be derived from the current dataset. Any valuation conclusion at this stage would rest primarily on transaction history (the $36.5M total raised) rather than market-based peer calibration. Further data collection on comparable company financials is necessary to support a defensible valuation estimate.
